The '''Eureka Prizes''' are awarded annually by the [[Australian Museum]], [[Sydney]], to recognise individuals and organisations who have contributed to science and the understanding of science in Australia. They were founded in 1990 following a suggestion by science journalist [[Robyn Williams]].<ref>{{cite news |url=http://nla.gov.au/nla.news-article122387079 |author=Peter Pockley |author-link=Peter Pockley |title=Selinger wins a Eureka prize |newspaper=[[The Canberra Times]] |location=Australian Capital Territory, Australia |date=28 September 1991 |access-date=29 March 2020 |page=17 |via=Trove }}</ref>

As of 2024, there are 19 prizes awarded across four categories and a total of ${{Currency|180,000|AUD}} in prize money. The four categories are Research and Innovation, School Science, Science Engagement and Leadership.<ref>{{Cite web |title=2024 Australian Museum Eureka Prizes finalists |url=https://australian.museum/blog/science/2024-eureka-prizes-finalists/ |access-date=2024-09-16 |website=The Australian Museum |language=en}}</ref>

extract:
The Eureka Prizes are awarded annually by the Australian Museum, Sydney, to recognise individuals and organisations who have contributed to science and the understanding of science in Australia. They were founded in 1990 following a suggestion by science journalist Robyn Williams.
As of 2024, there are 19 prizes awarded across four categories and a total of $A$180,000 in prize money. The four categories are Research and Innovation, School Science, Science Engagement and Leadership.
